verdicts.reason: A puts the 'See the Flavours' CTA at the very top, so the reading order is backwards (action before message). The headline is broken into five ragged lines ('and a / little'), and the italic subline is blown up to nearly headline size, which flattens the hierarchy. B keeps the original order, but the subline sits right under the headline at almost the same size and nearly touches the side edges, and a large empty gap separates the text from a small CTA. B's problem is spacing, which is easier to fix than A's backwards reading order, so B is slightly less bad.
